[LAW] Personal jurisdiction over a nonresident defendant is constitutional when two conditions are met: (1) the defendant has established minimum contacts with the forum state and (2) the exercise of jurisdiction comports with traditional notions of fair play and substantial justice.
[LAW] The likelihood that personal jurisdiction can be constitutionally exercised is directly proportionate to the nature and quality of commercial activity that an entity conducts over the Internet.

[INFERRED] Whether a state coastal regulation that completely deprives beachfront property of all economically beneficial or productive use constitutes a categorical regulatory taking requiring just compensation under the Fifth Amendment.
[INFERRED] A regulation that completely deprives an owner of all economically beneficial or productive use of property effects a total regulatory taking for which the government must pay just compensation, unless the restriction is independently justified by background principles of nuisance and property law (505 U. S. 1003, 1019).
[INFERRED] Here, the family owns beachfront lots purchased as an investment, and a new state coastal regulation completely bars any permanent habitable structure on the lots to prevent erosion. Appraisals confirm that the regulation has stripped the property of all economically viable use, leaving a nominal resale value of approximately $5,000 compared to the $500,000 purchase price. Because this action denies the owners all economically beneficial use of the land, it mirrors the total regulatory taking recognized in Lucas v. South Carolina Coastal Council.
[INFERRED] The state's coastal regulation constitutes a categorical regulatory taking, and the family is entitled to seek just compensation.
[INFERRED] The State will argue that the coastal regulation does not effect a categorical taking because the restriction is a temporary or partial measure aimed at preventing coastal erosion under its legitimate police powers, requiring the claim to be evaluated under the ad hoc balancing test of Penn Central rather than as a per se taking.
